category.text: AI_ML_Topics/ML in Supply Chain Case Study

name.text: Core flaw of predict-then-optimize (PTO) in supply chain planning

questiontext.text: What is a core flaw of the traditional "predict-then-optimize" (PTO) approach to supply chain planning?

answer.text: It requires too much data to function properly
It makes decisions based solely on average cost
It depends on forecasts that are often misaligned across stakeholders
It ignores customer-level demand patterns

questiontext.text: In the case study of the semiconductor equipment company, how did Optimal Machine Learning (OML) improve inventory performance?

answer.text: It fully eliminated the need for inventory
It increased fill rates while reducing inventory investment
It replaced all human decision-making with automation
It decreased product availability to control costs

questiontext.text: Why do conventional scenario planning efforts often fall short in supply chains?

answer.text: They ignore cost data from suppliers
They focus only on profitability metrics
They lack the granularity to assess product, customer, and regional impacts
They are based on real-time IoT data

questiontext.text: What key feature of the digital twin in OML enhances stakeholder trust and buy-in?

answer.text: Ability to control all external supplier behavior
Black-box model that hides internal logic
Visualization of historical decision impacts vs. actual results
Randomized forecasting for scenario diversity

questiontext.text: What organizational change is critical to successfully implementing OML?

answer.text: Outsourcing planning to third-party vendors
Replacing all ERP systems with neural networks
Redesigning the S&OP process for faster cycles and broader participation
Only using data scientists to define inventory policies

questiontext.text: What is a key organizational risk when companies delegate ML-based supply chain planning solely to data scientists?

answer.text: Data scientists often prioritize speed over accuracy
Supply chain complexity leads to overfitting in ML models
Data scientists may lack domain knowledge critical for capturing planning constraints
ML models become expensive to maintain without IT involvement

questiontext.text: Which factor most significantly hinders the real-time adoption of ML-driven decisions in supply chain operations?

answer.text: Inadequate cloud infrastructure
Lack of trust in black-box model recommendations among stakeholders
Poor historical sales data quality
Model latency during computation
